about: Approximate starting setups per car category. Starting points, not optimal tunes. Values are imperial (psi, in); sliders are unitless. basis: published = an FM2023 source, carried_over = an FM7/Forza Horizon source, principles = general setup logic without a published number.

gearing.final_drive.note: Start from the ratio the build gives you. QuickTune FM2023: with Forza's standard race gearbox, final drive ≈ 4.25 + 0.01 × (400 − hp) ÷ 6; with any other race gearbox, lower it by 0.01 per 6 hp added over stock. Then check the longest straight: on the limiter before the braking point → lower it (longer); top gear never near the limiter → raise it (shorter).

brake.balance.note: Balance is % to the front. ForzaTune and posted tunes run 100% pressure (set it so the wheels lock only in the last 10–15% of pedal travel); QuickTune runs 125% for road cars and 145% for race cars. Race and high-performance cars: QuickTune 44%, posted tunes 44–47%.

brake.pressure.note: Balance is % to the front. ForzaTune and posted tunes run 100% pressure (set it so the wheels lock only in the last 10–15% of pedal travel); QuickTune runs 125% for road cars and 145% for race cars. Race and high-performance cars: QuickTune 44%, posted tunes 44–47%.

diff.accel_rear.note: FM2023 likes more acceleration lock than FM7. Sources: QuickTune (per car type), ForzaTune (RWD 40–60 / 20–40, FWD 20–30 / 0–10), a community note (RWD 50–90 / 0–25) and posted tunes (65–70 / 15–18). QuickTune GP cars 44–52 / 0.

diff.decel_rear.note: FM2023 likes more acceleration lock than FM7. Sources: QuickTune (per car type), ForzaTune (RWD 40–60 / 20–40, FWD 20–30 / 0–10), a community note (RWD 50–90 / 0–25) and posted tunes (65–70 / 15–18). QuickTune GP cars 44–52 / 0.

notes: Pre-1968 cars have no wings; ignore the aero lines for them.
The 1920s–40s Grand Prix cars run on vintage tires: start 2–3 psi lower.
